newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Democrats win local elections-official.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Democrats win local elections-official.

text.p: Albania's ruling Democratic Party won the lion's share of town halls and communes in last month's local elections, final official figures provided by the country's Central Election Commission on Saturday showed.
"The Democratic Party has won 58 out of 64 town halls and 267 communes out of a total of 310," commission chairman Nestor Thereska told Reuters.

Thereska said the key opposition Socialist Party had won only four town halls. One mayoralty went to an independent candidate and another to a candidate from a rightist coalition between the Monarchy Party and the National Front Party.

The key opposition Socialists won 15 of the rural communes. A handful of right-wing parties won the remaining 14 communes whereas five were won by independent candidates and nine by the ethnic Greek Human Rights party.

The local elections decided the political make-up of the Balkan nation's 64 city halls, 310 rural communes and 36 regional councils. Turnout in both rounds on October 20 and 27 was 72 percent, the commission said.
The Democrats' 90 percent share of city halls compares to 51 percent they won in the last local polls, held in 1992 shortly after they ousted the Socialists from power on a national level.
President Sali Berisha's Democrats won 86 percent of communes, up from 37 percent, and 53 percent of the vote for regional councils compared with 43 percent last time.
The Socialists won six percent of city halls, down from 35 percent, and five percent of communes, down from 45 percent. They gained 31 percent of regional councils compared to 41 percent in 1992.

The polls were seen as a litmus test for Albania's fledgling democracy after most opposition parties including the Socialists boycotted a general election in May and June over allegations of ballot-rigging in favour of the Democrats.
The Council of Europe delegation that monitored both rounds of the local polls said it was satisfied with the conduct of the elections although it noted some irregularities.
The United States also said it was satisfied with the poll but urged the former Stalinist country to draw up a new constitution and stage fresh national elections soon.
President Berisha has insisted the next general elections will be held on schedule in four years time.
